headline: Red Sox grit out a massive win in Baltimore
morning_brew: That was the kind of win that makes you wanna run through a brick wall. Suarez was an absolute machine, giving us seven scoreless innings and keeping the Orioles completely off balance, which is exactly the performance we needed with the postseason race tightening up like a pair of skinny jeans. When you're sitting in the second wild card spot, you don't ask how, you just take the win and keep moving. It wasn't pretty, it wasn't a blowout, but it got the job done and keeps us in position with twenty games to play.

The benches cleared over that Blaze Alexander slide, and honestly, it’s about damn time this team showed a little bit of a pulse. My mother told me this morning that if the team plays with that kind of grit for the rest of the month, she might actually stop complaining about the bullpen. I told her I’d believe it when I see it, but I’ve gotta admit, watching them stand up for each other in Baltimore had me feeling better about this group than I have in a while. It’s the first time in weeks I haven’t felt like I was watching a slow motion car crash.

We're sitting five games up on the next chaser, but I'm not getting comfortable until we see that clinched tag. We've got another big one tonight at Camden Yards, and if the bats can give us a little more support than the single run we scraped together yesterday, maybe we can make this weekend series a statement. I’m knocking on wood every time I think about the standings, because around here, you never take anything for granted, especially with the way the Duck Boat fund has been bouncing around lately.

news_digest.headline: Benches clear in Red Sox-Orioles after Blaze Alexander's hard slide
news_digest.dans_take: Seeing them trade shoves in Baltimore was the most heart I’ve seen this team show all year.

trend_watch.dans_take: He pitched like his life depended on it, and honestly, for our postseason hopes, it kinda does.
He is carrying this lineup on his back like he’s hauling my groceries up three flights of stairs.
A rare night where the arson squad actually put the fire out instead of fanning the flames.
